experiment: Independent replication at T 0.6 of the stratified post-minus-pre paired gap (RL plain minus base cue) on the clean harder 328, matched on RL answer length, using different samples and a different decoding setting from tests.json.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_hard.jsonl (base, cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (RL step 2,800, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). If a file has more than one row per unique_id, keep the row with the smallest sample value. Keep only unique_ids whose flag == 'none' in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json, join the two files on unique_id, and drop any unique_id missing from either file. Source label from rln3_overlap.json: post = AIME 2025 or HMMT Feb 2025; pre = every other source. right = (score == 1), using the stored v1 score field; cap hits and rows with no extracted answer count as their stored score (0 if score is null). Strata: sort the joined problems by the RL row's n_generated ascending, break ties by unique_id ascending, and cut into 4 consecutive groups of equal size (the remainder goes to the last group). In each stratum s and group g (post/pre), d_gs = mean over problems of (RL right - base right). w_s = (number of post problems in s) / (number of post problems). Drop any stratum that has post problems but no pre problems, and renormalise w over the remaining strata. G_g = sum_s w_s * d_gs. Statistic = 100 * (G_post - G_pre), in points.

experiment: Independent replication at T 0.6 of the both-right base/RL length comparison: median log length ratio, pre-cutoff minus post-cutoff, on the clean harder 328.
recipe: Same two files, row choice, 328 filter, join, drops and post/pre labels as the first test here (r3/base-01 F_hard.jsonl base cue; r3/s2800-01 P_hard.jsonl RL plain). Keep problems where score == 1 (stored v1) in both rows and cap_hit is false in both rows. For each kept problem, r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Statistic = median of r over kept pre problems minus median of r over kept post problems (for an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values). If no post problem is kept, recompute with the cap_hit condition removed, keeping score == 1 in both rows.
unit: difference of median log length ratios

experiment: MATH-500: per-token entropy of the RL model's own short right answers relative to its own long right answers (the RL-side counterpart of test 3).
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (key per_row, list T2) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. For each T2 row, per-token entropy e = sum_entropy_own / n_own. Drop rows with n_own == 0 or missing. Join with per_problem.json on problem_index. Keep problems with t2_right true and t2_cap_hit false. short = t2_generated_tokens <= 2000; long = t2_generated_tokens > 2000. Statistic = median e over short / median e over long (for an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values).

experiment: MATH-500, 4 independent samples per model at T 1.0: on problems that both models solve every time and where the base's typical answer is short, how much the base's answer length varies across its own samples, relative to how much RL's varies (median log ratio of coefficients of variation).
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (base) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (RL). Use only rows with attempt == 0. For each model and problem_index, collect the attempt-0 rows for samples 0, 1, 2 and 3. Keep a problem only if both models have all four attempt-0 rows, and every one of those 8 rows has score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit false. Missing rows exclude the problem; there are no ties to break. For each kept problem and model, take the 4 values of n_new, and set CV = (population standard deviation, ddof = 0) / (mean). Drop any problem where either model's CV is 0. Short problems are those where the median of the base's 4 n_new values (the mean of the two middle values) is <= 2000. For each short problem, compute L = ln(CV_base / CV_RL). Statistic = median of L over short problems (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values).

experiment: MATH-500, same 4-sample rows: base-versus-RL length variability on short problems minus the same on long problems (difference in median log CV ratios).
recipe: Same files, attempt-0 rows, kept problems (all 8 rows score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit false), CV definition, zero-CV drops and L = ln(CV_base / CV_RL) as in the first test here. Short = median of the base's 4 n_new values <= 2000; long = that median > 2000. Statistic = (median L over short problems) - (median L over long problems), with each median taken as in the first test (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values).

experiment: Does pre-loop compressibility predict a later rule-A loop in cued base answers at T 0.6 / top-p 1.0?
recipe: File iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (run_cell rows, 500 MATH-500 answers). Keep rows with len(text) >= 6000 characters that either have loop_A false or have loop_A true with onset_A_char >= 7000 (rows with loop_A true and onset_A_char missing or below 7000 are dropped). For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:6000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:6000].encode('utf-8')). Statistic: AUROC of -s as a score for loop_A == true over the kept rows (Mann-Whitney form, ties count 0.5). Cap hits are not used as the label; only loop_A is. Report the number of kept rows and positives.

experiment: Is the cued base's opening text at T 0.6 more self-similar than RL's opening text on the same problem?
recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base, cue) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (RL step 2,800, plain). For each pair compute rB = ratio(base.text[:3000]) and rR = ratio(rl.text[:3000]), with ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')). Score 1 if rB < rR, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: mean score over kept pairs. Report the number of kept pairs.

experiment: Pooled within-problem concordance of length with wrongness for the cued base: over all (right, wrong) pairs of finished attempt-0 samples of the same problem, the fraction in which the wrong sample has more new tokens.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows whose score_v3 is null/missing. Group by problem_index. experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base and RL plain endpoints
recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T2 (RL plain) = s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl; T3 (base plain) = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. Use all rows of each file (500 each, cap hits included, no filtering; if a problem_index occurs twice keep the first row; missing rows are simply absent). For each row, rate = 1000 * (number of matches of the case-sensitive regex \bWait\b in the field text) / max(n_new, 1). Let m = median of the T2 rates (numpy.median). F_X = fraction of rows of file X with rate >= m (ties at m count as >=). Compute F_theta, F_T2, F_T3. Statistic S = (F_theta - F_T3) / (F_T2 - F_T3). Report S to 3 decimals.

experiment: Answer-format-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base
recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T3 = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. All rows, cap hits included; first row per problem_index. A row is an 'answer-line' row if its text field contains no occurrence of the substring \boxed AND at least one line of the text, after stripping leading whitespace and any leading '*' or '#' characters, starts with the case-sensitive string 'Answer:'. s_X = (answer-line rows of X) / (rows of X). Statistic P = 1 - s_theta / s_T3. If s_T3 < 0.05 the statistic is undefined.

experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_cue against the cued base and RL cue endpoints
recipe: Files: theta0.25_cue = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029/answers.jsonl; RL cue = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985/answers.jsonl; T1 (base cue) = s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. experiment: MATH-500: share of RL's wrong finished samples whose answer equals one of the base's wrong finished answers on the same problem
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (base) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (RL). Keep rows with attempt == 0 only (4 samples per problem per model). A row is 'answered' iff cap_hit is false and extracted_v3 is a non-empty string after normalisation; a row is 'wrong' iff answered and score_v3 == 0. Normalise extracted_v3 by: delete all whitespace; strip leading/trailing '$'; replace '\dfrac' and '\tfrac' with '\frac'; delete '\left' and '\right'; delete one trailing '.'. Base wrong set W_b(p) = set of normalised extracted_v3 of base wrong rows on problem_index p. Denominator: all RL wrong rows (all problems). Numerator: RL wrong rows whose normalised extracted_v3 is in W_b(p) for their problem (empty W_b counts as no match). Missing problem rows count as empty sets. Report numerator/denominator.

experiment: MATH-500: on problems where the base repeats a wrong value, share of RL's wrong finished samples that equal the base's most frequent wrong value
recipe: Same files, filters, 'answered', 'wrong' and normalisation as the first prediction (attempt == 0 only). For each problem p, count normalised extracted_v3 strings over base wrong rows; p is an 'attractor problem' iff the maximum count is >= 2. Modal set M(p) = all strings with that maximum count (ties: all tied strings are in M(p)). Denominator: RL wrong rows on attractor problems. Numerator: those whose normalised extracted_v3 is in M(p). Report numerator/denominator; if the denominator is 0, report 0.

experiment: MATH-500: RL vote fix rate on base-vote-wrong problems where the base has a repeated wrong value

experiment: Standardised paired gap (RL plain minus base cue, grader v3) on the clean harder 328, post-cutoff problems minus pre-cutoff problems, matched on RL answer length.
recipe: Files: s3 results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and .../abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain). Join on unique_id and drop any unique_id missing from either file. Source label of each unique_id: as recorded in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the file whose flag == 'none' items define the 328). post = AIME 2025 or HMMT Feb 2025; pre = every other source. right = score_v3 == 1 as stored; cap hits keep their stored score_v3 (normally 0). Strata: sort the joined problems by the RL row's n_generated ascending, break ties by unique_id ascending, and cut into 4 consecutive groups of equal size (the remainder goes to the last group). In each stratum s and group g, d_gs = mean over problems of (RL right - base right). Weights w_s = (number of post problems in s) / (number of post problems). Drop any stratum that has post problems but no pre problems, and renormalise w over the remaining strata. G_g = sum_s w_s * d_gs. Statistic = 100 * (G_post - G_pre), in points.

experiment: On harder-328 problems both models solve, the base's answer length relative to RL's, pre-cutoff minus post-cutoff.
recipe: Same two files, join, drops and post/pre labels as the first prediction. Keep problems where score_v3 == 1 in both rows and cap_hit is false in both rows. If fewer than 5 post problems are kept, the statistic is recorded as missing and the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Share of step-400 cap hits that are rule-A loops, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.

experiment: Within one problem, cued base at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95: is the opening of a sample that hit the cap more compressible than the opening of a fresh restart of the same problem that finished?

Define ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')) (Python zlib, level 9). For each problem_index in K_fresh, take its K_fresh row; if there are several, take the one with the lowest sample. Keep the problem only if that K row has cap_hit false, len(text) >= 3000, and not (loop_A true with onset_A_char missing or < 3000). Drop the problem if there is no such F row, if len(F.text) < 3000, or if ratio(F.text[:8000]) < 0.10. For each kept problem compute rF = ratio(F.text[:3000]) and rK = ratio(K.text[:3000]). Score 1 if rF < rK, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: mean score over kept problems. Report the number of kept problems.

experiment: Does early compressibility still predict a rule-A loop once problems are matched on difficulty (AUROC computed within quartiles of RL answer length)?
recipe: Files iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl. Compute q1, q2, q3 = numpy.percentile(d over kept rows, [25, 50, 75]) (default linear interpolation). Stratum 1 = d <= q1, 2 = q1 < d <= q2, 3 = q2 < d <= q3, 4 = d > q3. Within each stratum, form every pair of one row with loop_A true and one row with loop_A false; a pair scores 1 if s_pos < s_neg, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: total score over all within-stratum pairs divided by the total number of within-stratum pairs (a stratum with no positives or no negatives contributes nothing).
